You are synthesizing 2 independent code review findings.
Your mission: 1. VERIFY each issue raised by reviewers - Cross-reference with project_context.md (ground truth) - Cross-reference with git diff and source files - Identify false positives (issues that aren't real problems) - Confirm valid issues with evidence
2. PRIORITIZE real issues by severity - Critical: Security vulnerabilities, data corruption risks - High: Bugs, logic errors, missing error handling - Medium: Code quality issues, performance concerns - Low: Style issues, minor improvements
3. SYNTHESIZE findings - Merge duplicate issues from different reviewers - Note reviewer consensus (if 3+ agree, high confidence) - Highlight unique insights from individual reviewers
4. --- name: bmad-code-review-synthesis description: 'Master synthesis of multiple code-review reviewer outputs. Verifies findings, dismisses false positives, applies SOURCE-CODE fixes (not story changes), and emits a machine-readable resolution contract for downstream automation. Use after running code-review across multiple LLM providers.' ---
# Code Review Synthesis Workflow
**Goal:** Synthesize 2+ independent code-review reviewer findings, apply verified source-code fixes, run tests after each fix group, and emit a synthesis report with a machine-readable resolution block.
**Your Role:** Master synthesis agent for source-code fixes.
- All inputs (project context, anonymized reviewer outputs, git diff, modified source files, story file, optional Deep Verify findings, optional Security findings, optional TEA test-review findings) are EMBEDDED in the CONTEXT section — do NOT attempt to read upstream files. - You DO have WRITE permission for SOURCE CODE files. You DO have permission to update the story's "Dev Agent Record" subsections (task checkboxes, completion notes, file list). You do NOT modify the story's context body (AC, Dev Notes content). - Communicate all responses in `English`; emit the synthesis report in `English`.
## Conventions
- Bare paths resolve from the skill root. - `/private/var/folders/c8/4hyhkyxn3xz219khx9yp4l100000gp/T/bmad-assist-snapshot-projects/bmad-code-review-synthesis/proj/.claude/skills/bmad-code-review-synthesis` resolves to this skill's installed directory (where `customize.toml` lives). - `/private/var/folders/c8/4hyhkyxn3xz219khx9yp4l100000gp/T/bmad-assist-snapshot-projects/bmad-code-review-synthesis/proj`-prefixed paths resolve from the project working directory. - `bmad-code-review-synthesis` resolves to the skill directory's basename.
## On Activation
### Step 1: Resolve the Workflow Block
Run: `python3 /private/var/folders/c8/4hyhkyxn3xz219khx9yp4l100000gp/T/bmad-assist-snapshot-projects/bmad-code-review-synthesis/proj/_bmad/scripts/resolve_customization.py --skill /private/var/folders/c8/4hyhkyxn3xz219khx9yp4l100000gp/T/bmad-assist-snapshot-projects/bmad-code-review-synthesis/proj/.claude/skills/bmad-code-review-synthesis --key workflow`
**If the script fails**, resolve the `workflow` block yourself by reading these three files in base → team → user order and applying the same structural merge rules as the resolver:
1. `/private/var/folders/c8/4hyhkyxn3xz219khx9yp4l100000gp/T/bmad-assist-snapshot-projects/bmad-code-review-synthesis/proj/.claude/skills/bmad-code-review-synthesis/customize.toml` — defaults 2. `/private/var/folders/c8/4hyhkyxn3xz219khx9yp4l100000gp/T/bmad-assist-snapshot-projects/bmad-code-review-synthesis/proj/_bmad/custom/bmad-code-review-synthesis.toml` — team overrides 3. `/private/var/folders/c8/4hyhkyxn3xz219khx9yp4l100000gp/T/bmad-assist-snapshot-projects/bmad-code-review-synthesis/proj/_bmad/custom/bmad-code-review-synthesis.user.toml` — personal overrides
Any missing file is skipped. Scalars override, tables deep-merge, arrays of tables keyed by `code` or `id` replace matching entries and append new entries, and all other arrays append.
### Step 2: Execute Prepend Steps
Execute each entry in `` in order before proceeding.
### Step 3: Load Persistent Facts
Treat every entry in `- file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md` as foundational context you carry for the rest of the workflow run. Entries prefixed `file:` are paths or globs under `/private/var/folders/c8/4hyhkyxn3xz219khx9yp4l100000gp/T/bmad-assist-snapshot-projects/bmad-code-review-synthesis/proj` — load the referenced contents as facts. All other entries are facts verbatim.
### Step 4: Load Config
Load config from `/private/var/folders/c8/4hyhkyxn3xz219khx9yp4l100000gp/T/bmad-assist-snapshot-projects/bmad-code-review-synthesis/proj/_bmad/bmm/config.yaml` and resolve:
- `project_name`, `user_name` - `communication_language`, `document_output_language` - `planning_artifacts`, `implementation_artifacts` - `date` as system-generated current datetime
### Step 5: Greet the User
Greet `{user_name}`, speaking in `English`.
### Step 6: Execute Append Steps
Execute each entry in `- HEADLESS MULTI-LLM CODE REVIEW SYNTHESIS — Authoritative Overrides
You are running in headless multi-LLM orchestration mode. All inputs are pre-computed and fully embedded in this prompt's <context> section. There is no user to ask; do not request clarification or that any input be re-run.
Embedded inputs (use these directly): - Reviewer reports → <file> entries with the per-validator report content (Validator A, Validator B, …) - Pre-calculated Evidence Score → <!-- PRE-CALCULATED EVIDENCE SCORE --> block (deterministic — DO NOT recalculate) - Deep Verify findings → embedded in context - Security findings → embedded in context - Story file, code files, architecture → other <file> entries
Skill overrides: 1. Skip all interactive gates. Ignore: <ask> blocks, "HALT. Ask the user", "[Y] Yes / [N] No" prompts, "Should I", "Before I proceed", "What do you want", numbered selection menus, CHECKPOINT halts requesting human confirmation, "wait for user input", and any prose Tier-N "Ask" cascades. There is no user. 2. The reviewer outputs are final — synthesize directly from them. DO NOT ask for them to be re-run, expanded, or re-scoped. 3. Use the pre-calculated Evidence Score and verdict from the <!-- PRE-CALCULATED EVIDENCE SCORE --> block directly. DO NOT recalculate; the orchestrator computes these deterministically. 4. If reviewer output is incomplete, ambiguous, or contradictory, note this in your synthesis (e.g. with verdict UNKNOWN or CONCERNS) but proceed to a final report. Do not stall on missing context. 5. Do not ask for clarification under any circumstances. Make the most defensible reading and continue.` in order.
Activation is complete. Begin the workflow below.
## Input Files
| Input | Description | Path Pattern(s) | Load Strategy | |-------|-------------|------------------|---------------| | project_context | Ground-truth conventions for verifying claims | `/private/var/folders/c8/4hyhkyxn3xz219khx9yp4l100000gp/T/bmad-assist-snapshot-projects/bmad-code-review-synthesis/proj/**/project-context.md` | EMBEDDED | | reviews | Anonymized reviewer outputs (Reviewer A, B, C, D, ...) | injected via `[Reviewer X]` virtual paths | EMBEDDED | | git_diff | Diff of changes under review | injected as `[git-diff]` virtual path | EMBEDDED | | source_files | Modified source files (max 3, prioritized) | injected via real file paths | EMBEDDED | | story | Story file (for Dev Agent Record updates) | `{implementation_artifacts}/10-1-*.md` | EMBEDDED | | deep_verify | Optional Deep Verify static-analysis findings | injected as `[Deep Verify Findings]` | EMBEDDED_IF_PRESENT | | security | Optional security agent findings | injected as `[Security Findings]` | EMBEDDED_IF_PRESENT | | tea | Optional TEA test-review context | injected via virtual paths | EMBEDDED_IF_PRESENT |
## Execution
<workflow>
<critical>You are the MASTER SYNTHESIS agent for CODE REVIEW findings.</critical> <critical>You have WRITE PERMISSION to modify SOURCE CODE files and the story's Dev Agent Record subsections (task checkboxes, completion notes, file list).</critical> <critical>DO NOT modify story context (AC, Dev Notes content) — only the Dev Agent Record sections.</critical> <critical>All upstream context is EMBEDDED below — do NOT attempt to read source files outside the embedded set unless directly applying an Edit.</critical>
<step n="1" goal="Analyze reviewer findings"> <action>Read every embedded `[Reviewer X]` block.</action> <action>For each issue raised: - Cross-reference against the embedded project_context.md, story file, and source-code snippets. - Note reviewer consensus: 3+ reviewers agreeing = high-confidence; 1-2 reviewers = extra scrutiny. - Group related findings that address the same underlying problem. </action> </step>
<step n="1.5" goal="Review Deep Verify code analysis (when present)"> <check if="[Deep Verify Findings] section present"> <critical>DV analyzed the actual source code with static-analysis patterns. DV findings often catch issues reviewers miss; treat pattern IDs (CC-* concurrency, SEC-* security, DB-* storage, DT-* transformation, GEN-* general quality) as higher-confidence anchors.</critical> <action>Triage by severity: - **CRITICAL** — security vulns, race conditions, resource leaks → must address. - **ERROR** — bugs, missing error handling, boundary issues → should address. - **WARNING** — code-quality concerns → consider. </action> <action>Cross-reference with reviewer findings: - Both flag → highest confidence; prioritize fix. - DV-only → verify via source; DV provides precise line numbers. - Reviewer-only → may be design / logic issues DV cannot detect. </action> </check> </step>
<step n="2" goal="Verify issues and identify false positives"> <action>For each issue, verify against the embedded code context: - Does the issue actually exist in the current code? - Is the suggested fix appropriate for the codebase patterns? - Would the fix introduce regressions? </action> <action>Document false positives with explicit reasoning: why the reviewer was wrong, what evidence contradicts the finding, references to specific code or project_context.md patterns.</action> </step>
<step n="3" goal="Prioritize by severity"> <action>Assign severity to verified issues: - **Critical** — security vulns, data corruption, crashes. - **High** — bugs that break functionality, performance regressions. - **Medium** — code-quality issues, missing error handling. - **Low** — style, minor improvements, documentation. </action> <action>Order fixes by severity: Critical → High → Medium → Low.</action> <action>Disputed issues (reviewers disagree, no clear evidence either way) → mark for manual resolution; do not apply.</action> </step>
<step n="4" goal="Apply source-code fixes"> <critical>SOURCE CODE modification only — never modify the story's content body.</critical> <critical>Before using Edit, ALWAYS Read the target file first. Use the EXACT content from the Read output as `old_string` (NOT content from this prompt). If the Read output is truncated, use offset/limit to locate the target section.</critical> <critical>After EACH logical fix group (related changes), run: `pytest -q --tb=line --no-header`. NEVER proceed to the next fix while tests are red — either revert or adjust until green.</critical>
<action>For each verified issue, in severity order: 1. Identify the source file(s) from reviewer findings (and DV line numbers when available). 2. Apply the fix with Edit; change ONLY the identified issue. Preserve code style, indentation, surrounding context. 3. Log the change for the synthesis report (file, before/after snippet, what changed). 4. After each logical group: run tests. On failure, analyze which fix broke them, revert or adjust, re-run, log a partial-fix entry in the report. </action> <action>Atomic commit guidance for the user: `fix(component): brief description (synthesis-10.1)`. Group fixes by severity and affected component; never commit unrelated changes together.</action> </step>
<step n="5" goal="Refactor only if tightly scoped"> <critical>Refactor ONLY code directly related to applied fixes, and ONLY in files already modified in step 4.</critical> <action>If the same fix appeared 2+ times across files modified in step 4, extract common logic to a shared function/module and update all call sites in those modified files. Run tests after refactoring.</action> <action>DO NOT refactor: unrelated code, files untouched in step 4, "could be improved" patterns. Surface broader refactorings as "Suggested future improvements" in the report — leave them for a dedicated story.</action> </step>
<step n="6" goal="Generate synthesis report"> <critical>When updating story file Dev Agent Record sections, use atomic write (temp file + rename).</critical> <action>Update the story's Dev Agent Record sections ONLY: - Mark completed tasks `[x]` if a fix addresses them. - Append a brief summary to "Completion Notes List" describing the changes applied. - Update the file list with all modified files. </action> <critical>Your synthesis report MUST be wrapped in the `<!-- CODE_REVIEW_SYNTHESIS_START -->` / `<!-- CODE_REVIEW_SYNTHESIS_END -->` markers. Both METRICS_JSON and SYNTHESIS_RESOLUTION blocks MUST appear BEFORE the END marker.</critical>
<output-format> <!-- CODE_REVIEW_SYNTHESIS_START --> ## Synthesis Summary [Brief overview: X issues verified, Y false positives dismissed, Z fixes applied to source files]
## Validations Quality [Per reviewer: id (A, B, C, ...), 1-10 quality score, brief assessment. Do NOT attempt to identify providers.]
## Issues Verified (by severity)
### Critical [Format: "- **Issue**: Description | **Source**: Reviewer(s) | **File**: path | **Fix**: What was changed". If none: "No critical issues identified."]
### High [Same format]
### Medium [Same format]
### Low [Same format; note any deferred items]
## Issues Dismissed [Format: "- **Claimed Issue**: Description | **Raised by**: Reviewer(s) | **Dismissal Reason**: Why this is incorrect"] [If none: "No false positives identified."]
## Changes Applied [For each source-code change: **File**: [path/to/file.py] **Change**: [Brief description] **Before**: ``` [2-3 lines of original code] ``` **After**: ``` [2-3 lines of updated code] ``` ] [If no changes: "No source code changes required."]
## Deep Verify Integration [Only if [Deep Verify Findings] was present.]
### DV Findings Fixed [Format: "- **{ID}** [{SEVERITY}]: {Title} | **File**: {path} | **Fix**: {What was changed}"]
### DV Findings Dismissed [Format: "- **{ID}** [{SEVERITY}]: {Title} | **Reason**: {Why this is not an issue}"]
### DV-Reviewer Overlap [Findings flagged by both DV and reviewers — highest-confidence fixes.] [If no DV findings: "Deep Verify did not produce findings for this story."]
## Security Analysis [Only when [Security Findings] is embedded. Summarize findings addressed (with applied fixes), dismissed (with justification), deferred (with reasoning). HIGH-severity findings with confidence ≥ 0.8 MUST be explicitly addressed (fix or detailed justification for disagreement). When `security_review_status` indicates timeout, lead the section with: "SECURITY REVIEW NOT COMPLETED — security analysis timed out, manual security review recommended".]
## Files Modified [Plain list of every file modified in step 4 / step 5.] [If none: "No files modified."]
## Suggested Future Improvements [Broader refactorings or improvements identified but NOT applied.] [Format: "- **Scope**: Description | **Rationale**: Why deferred | **Effort**: Estimated complexity"] [If none: "No future improvements identified."]
## Test Results [Summary of the final pytest run.] - Tests passed: X - Tests failed: 0 (required for completion)
## Metrics JSON [Machine-readable benchmarking block — MUST be valid JSON between the markers, with EXACTLY two top-level keys: "quality" and "consensus".] <!-- METRICS_JSON_START --> { "quality": { "actionable_ratio": 0.0, "specificity_score": 0.0, "evidence_quality": 0.0, "follows_template": true, "internal_consistency": 0.0 }, "consensus": { "agreed_findings": 0, "unique_findings": 0, "disputed_findings": 0, "missed_findings": 0, "agreement_score": 0.0, "false_positive_count": 0 } } <!-- METRICS_JSON_END -->
## Resolution [Machine-readable resolution block — MUST appear BEFORE CODE_REVIEW_SYNTHESIS_END. Counts derived from your synthesis above: - verified_critical / verified_high — Critical / High issues VERIFIED (not dismissed) across reviewers. - fixed_critical / fixed_high — Critical / High issues you APPLIED FIXES for in this round. - remaining_critical / remaining_high — verified minus fixed (≥ 0). - resolution: "resolved" when remaining_critical == 0 AND remaining_high == 0 "rework" when remaining_critical > 0 OR remaining_high > 0 "halt" when you cannot reliably determine counts Do NOT omit any field.] <!-- SYNTHESIS_RESOLUTION_START --> resolution: {resolved|rework|halt} verified_critical: {N} verified_high: {N} fixed_critical: {N} fixed_high: {N} remaining_critical: {N} remaining_high: {N} <!-- SYNTHESIS_RESOLUTION_END --> <!-- CODE_REVIEW_SYNTHESIS_END --> </output-format> </step>
<step n="6.5" goal="Append Review Findings section to story file"> <critical>This section enables `dev_story` to detect that a code review has occurred and extract action items. APPEND a new `### Review Findings` heading at the end of the `## Tasks / Subtasks` section — do NOT replace existing content. This matches the upstream BMAD `bmad-code-review` step-04-present convention.</critical>
<action>Determine the evidence verdict from your analysis: - **REJECT** when remaining Critical or High issues exist. - **PASS** when all Critical and High verified issues are fixed. - **UNCERTAIN** when low-severity issues dominate or evidence is ambiguous. </action> <action>Map verdict to outcome: - PASS → "Approved" - REJECT → "Changes Requested" - UNCERTAIN → "Approved with Reservations" </action> <action>Append the following block to the story file at the end of the `## Tasks / Subtasks` section. Each rework round adds a new `### Review Findings` heading; previous rounds remain in place: ``` ### Review Findings - **Date:** {current_date} - **Reviewer:** AI Code Review Synthesis - **Outcome:** {Approved|Changes Requested|Approved with Reservations} - **Issues Found:** {total_verified_issues} - **Issues Fixed:** {fixes_applied_count} - **Action Items Created:** {remaining_unfixed_count} ``` </action>
<critical>When the verdict is REJECT, you MUST create Review Follow-ups tasks. The "Action Items Created" count MUST equal the number of unchecked `[ ] [Review][Patch]` and `[ ] [Review][Decision]` tasks emitted below. Do NOT skip this step. Do NOT claim all issues are fixed if you reported deferred items above.</critical> <action>Find the "## Tasks / Subtasks" section in the story file.</action> <action>Append a `#### Review Follow-ups (AI)` subsection. Use BMAD's `[Review][...]` tag taxonomy (NOT a legacy `[AI-Review]` tag) and embed the synthesis severity inline so dev-story can prioritize. Map verified-but-unfixed issues to tags as follows, ordered Critical → Low: - **CRITICAL / HIGH** verified-but-unfixed issues → `- [ ] [Review][Patch] {Title} [{file}:{line}] — {SEVERITY}: {one-line detail}` - **MEDIUM** issues that need a human call (rare in autonomous flow) → `- [ ] [Review][Decision] {Title} — {detail}` - **LOW / pre-existing / out-of-scope** items the synthesis chose not to fix → `- [x] [Review][Defer] {Title} [{file}:{line}] — deferred from AI review ({one-line reason})` </action>
<critical>ATDD DEFECT CHECK: Search test directories (`tests/**`) for `test.fixme()` calls in test files related to this story. Any remaining `test.fixme()` is a DEFECT — `dev_story` failed to activate ATDD RED-phase tests. If any remain, append: `- [ ] [Review][Patch] Activate ATDD tests [{test file paths}] — HIGH: convert all test.fixme() to test() and ensure they pass` Do NOT dismiss `test.fixme()` as "intentional TDD methodology". After `dev_story` completes, ALL story-related `test.fixme()` MUST be converted to `test()`.</critical> </step>
<step n="6.6" goal="Append deferred items to deferred-work.md"> <critical>Match BMAD's `bmad-code-review` step-04-present convention: every `[Review][Defer]` finding is also recorded in the project-wide deferred-work log so it survives outside the story file.</critical>
<action>If you emitted no `[Review][Defer]` items in step 6.5, skip this step.</action> <action>Resolve `{deferred_work_file}` = `{implementation_artifacts}/deferred-work.md`. Create the file if it does not exist (no header required — just bullets under per-review headings).</action> <action>Append a heading (do NOT replace existing headings) of the form: ``` ## Deferred from: code review of story-10.1 (2026-01-15) ``` </action> <action>Under that heading, write one bullet per `[Review][Defer]` finding from step 6.5, format: ``` - {Title} [{file}:{line}] — {one-line reason} ``` </action> </step>
<step n="6.7" goal="Update story status to reflect synthesis outcome"> <critical>Match upstream `bmad-code-review/step-04-present.md` (lines 87-105) convention: synthesis outcome MUST propagate to BOTH the story file's `Status:` frontmatter AND ``'s `development_status[10-1-initial-setup]`. Without this, story files appear stuck in `review` status indefinitely after the loop has moved on.</critical>
<action>Determine the new status based on the synthesis resolution from step 6: - **resolved** (all critical/high addressed, no remaining action items) → `{new_status}` = `done` - **rework** (action items remain; dev needs to address them) → `{new_status}` = `in-progress` - **halt** (uncertain evidence or max rework attempts reached) → `{new_status}` = `in-progress` </action>
<action>Update the story file's `Status:` frontmatter line: - Locate the `Status:` line near the top of the story file (typically line 3, between the title and the first `<!-- -->` comment). - Replace its value with `{new_status}`. Preserve all other frontmatter, comments, and content unchanged. - Save the story file. </action>
<!-- managed programmatically by bmad-assist --> </step>
